newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSOPAK CAPITAL RAISE PLAN TECHNICAL - CEO.
newsitem.headline: CSOPAK CAPITAL RAISE PLAN TECHNICAL - CEO.

text.p: Hungarian retail group Csopak Szovetkezeti Rt said on Wednesday that its planned minimum 250 million forint capital increase would have a technical nature, without drawing fresh money into the group.
"This is a formal capital increase," Gyorgy Markovszky, Csopak's CEO told Reuters. "Local government shareholders of our subsidiary Komfort wished to swap their stocks to Csopak shares."
Komfort is a household chemicals trading company, majority owned by Csopak.
Markovszky said the share issue will not provide Csopak with fresh capital. "They give their Komfort shares and recieve Csopak shares," Markovszky said.
The planned private capital raise will be on the agenda of Csopak's extraordinary shareholders meeting on April 26.
Csopak's current issued share capital is 2.2 billion forints.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Csopak shares closed at 2,975 forints, down 115.
